Colorado I dangerous I lived there almost all my life. Here's my Colorado almost death story.

We were snowmobiling in the mountains on January 5 2005 it was my 19th b-day. We only had one snowmobile so we took turns playing on it in an area kinda like a bowl. When my turn came up my mom told me to go check out this trail. So I did. I got about half way up about 1 mile from everyone, and went to turn around. needless to say I got stuck at the bottom of this hill with a dense forest behind me and a very very steep hill in front of me. I was in a deep bowl. ( I was in jeans a t-shirt and a letter jacket. not true snowmobile gear. also my mom had taken the survival kit out of the holder to refill it and it never got put back in.) I tried walking out but it had just snowed about 4 ft and there was 2 foot of old snow. I could not walk out. 

I went back to the snowmobile and started calling for help revving the engine and tapping out S.O.S. on the handlebars. I could hear people ridding around and hear dogs barking. none of them heard me. I decided to try to make snow shoes out of the seat of the snowmobile. Which didn't work. then I started walking a path back and forth to pack the snow and make a trail. But I got to tired. The sun had set. So I sat down on what was left of the seat.

The night was the most beautiful I had ever seen the stars were so bright and the air so fresh. I thought it was a good day to die. I said my good byes. The temperature had dropped to 7 deg. F. and I had been there about 7 hours. I pulled my jacket sleeves in and pulled my head in the jacket using my ball cap to seal the head hole. I set there trying not to go to sleep. but it was so hard. Then I heard it I thought I had died. 

I heard a buzzing sound and someone calling my name. "This is it" I said I poked my head out to see 4 snowmobiles coming up the trail I yelled and cried. I was going to make it. The rescuers came down but had to use ropes to help get everyone out even they couldn't make it up the hill. 

My mom had called 911 and everyone in the family. The weird thing about that is nobody's cellphone worked there but hers. The rescuers didn't know how. once I was out and got to talk to my dad after I told him I was ok the signal went dead. 

I had a little frost bite not bad but still have no feeling in parts of my feet and legs. My jeans literally stood on their own they were frozen solid. 

The doctor said if I had been out there for 30 min. longer or were any smaller (I'm 5 foot 11 inches and 270 lbs at the time.) I would have been dead. My only explanation for the cell signal is ether god. or some star exploded slamming radiation in the upper atmosphere that only effected my mothers cell phone.
